layers.label: Galactic disk
layers.explanation: The thin, spinning plane containing nearly all the galaxy's stars and gas — about 1,000 light-years thick.

layers.label: Central bulge
layers.explanation: The crowded, bright hub around the galactic center, full of older stars.

hotspots.label: Central bar
hotspots.description: A bright bar of stars across the hub — the feature that makes the Milky Way a barred spiral.

hotspots.label: Spiral arm — star factory
hotspots.description: Density waves where gas piles up and ignites new stars — the blue, dusty winding arms you see in pictures.

hotspots.label: The Sun's position
hotspots.description: A small golden marker on a minor arm — about 26,000 light-years from the center.

hotspots.label: Galactic halo
hotspots.description: A sparse sphere of old globular clusters around the disk — some of the oldest objects in the galaxy.

hotspots.label: Galactic center
hotspots.description: The bright hub, hiding the radio source Sgr A* — a supermassive black hole of ~4 million solar masses.

visualStyleNotes: Angled barred-spiral pencil rendering: pale warm disk, golden bar, two blue-dusted arms, faint halo of small dots, all in the Anatomy Atelier clean-3D register — soft, not photorealistic. A toggle flips camera to an 'inside view' showing the band across the sky.
materialNotes: Stars: instanced meshes, density fading with radius. Arms: additive glow with density wave texture. Bar: brighter warm white. Halo: sparse faint point sprites. Sgr A* hotspot: no disk rendered, just the label.
assetBrief: Procedural Three.js scene: barred spiral with ~8k instanced star points, 2 arms, halo sphere of points, sun-position marker, inside-view toggle. Auto-rotate. Hotspots at listed positions.
